exposure: interval from skin incision to fetus delivery
outcome: Apgar score at one and 5 minutes
cohort: 1,029 very preterm infants (VPIs) born via cesarean section under 32 weeks' gestation
finding: General anesthesia during cesarean delivery was significantly associated with adverse outcomes in very preterm infants, including lower Apgar scores, increased need for resuscitation, and higher risk of severe neurological injury.
mod_finding: For VPIs delivered under general anesthesia, a prolonged interval from skin incision to fetus delivery was associated with a lower 5-minute Apgar score.
